topics.title: Cellular respiration sequence
topics.description: Glycolysis, Krebs cycle, then electron transport
topics.content:
## Key Ideas

Cellular respiration converts glucose into usable energy. Glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, and the electron transport chain work in sequence so the cell can harvest ATP.

## Step-by-Step Breakdown

First, glycolysis breaks glucose into pyruvate in the cytoplasm. Then the Krebs cycle oxidizes pyruvate-derived acetyl-CoA in the mitochondrial matrix. Finally, the electron transport chain uses the resulting NADH and FADH2 to make ATP.

## Common Mistakes

Students often confuse the Krebs cycle with glycolysis. Glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm, while the Krebs cycle happens in the mitochondrial matrix.
